landing.eyebrow: An Online Workspace for Web-Novel Writers
landing.heroTitle:
No video calls.
Just the feeling of writing side by side.
landing.heroBody: PoRoom is an online workspace where web-novel writers run a Pomodoro timer together in the same room. Serializing alone, without the feeling of being alone.
landing.ctaHint: All you need is a Google account — takes about 30 seconds.
landing.featuresTitle: What you can do on PoRoom

features.title: An online writing room
features.desc: No camera, no video call — just walk into a room and feel other web-novel writers sitting alongside you.

features.title: A synced Pomodoro timer
features.desc: See everyone's focus and break status in real time, so it's easier to stay locked in than writing alone.

features.title: Character counts by work
features.desc: Track each serialized work separately with its own character-count chart and progress.

features.title: Chat & whispers
features.desc: Chat freely in the room, or send a private whisper to just one participant when you need to.

features.title: Rankings, duels & challenges
features.desc: See how you rank by character count and focus time, challenge another writer to a duel, or join a group challenge.

features.title: Calendar, polls & boards
features.desc: Share your update deadlines on a calendar, gather opinions with polls, and browse the Free / Info / Recruiting boards.

landing.whyTitle: Why Pomodoro, why an online room
landing.whyPomodoroTitle: Why the Pomodoro Technique fits serialization so well
landing.whyPomodoroBody:
The Pomodoro Technique was developed in the late 1980s by Francesco Cirillo, an Italian developer who used a tomato-shaped kitchen timer (pomodoro is Italian for tomato). The method alternates 25 minutes of focused work with a 5-minute break, and today it's used far beyond its origins — by writers, students, developers, and office workers all over the world.

Serializing a web novel isn't a one-day sprint; it's a race that runs for months or years. How you handle today decides how the whole run goes. A goal like "5,000 characters today" can feel overwhelming, but broken into 25-minute blocks, all you have to do is press the timer once. The built-in breaks keep long sitting sessions from turning into burnout, and repeating the same rhythm day after day builds the habit of focusing the moment you sit down — a habit that outlasts any single day's willpower.
landing.whyRoomTitle: Why it feels like "together" without a single video call
landing.whyRoomBody:
Most of us have had the experience of somehow focusing better at a library or a study café. That effect has a name — "body doubling": just having someone else working alongside you raises your own focus and follow-through, which is also why online study communities have grown so popular.

The catch is that most web-novel writers work alone as freelancers, so that sense of "someone else is here too" rarely happens on its own. PoRoom recreates it without a camera or microphone — just the real-time focus and break status of everyone else in your room is enough to make you feel like you're not doing this alone.
landing.benefitsTitle: What changes when you keep coming back
benefits: Logging in at a set time becomes a routine, making it easier to keep your update schedule.
Your character count and focus time build up into charts, so you can actually see how much you've written instead of just guessing.
Rankings, duels, and challenges add just enough tension and fun to keep things interesting.
Chat and the feed naturally connect you with other writers in the same boat.

usageGuide.title: Forum
usageGuide.desc: The main screen. Browse open rooms and join one, or create your own with tags. Save the rooms you visit often to your favorites so you can find them instantly next time.

usageGuide.title: Room
usageGuide.desc: Everything lives here: participant cards, the Pomodoro timer, chat, and the character-count input. Start the timer and your focus status shows up in real time for everyone else in the room — plus a calendar, polls, and a board tab.

usageGuide.title: Feed
usageGuide.desc: Post a short update about your day and trade encouragement with other writers. Pick whichever category fits — Writing, Duel, Challenge, Submission, or Contest.

usageGuide.title: Challenge
usageGuide.desc: Create a 1-on-1 duel against another writer measured by character count or focus time (or join one with a code), and take part in recurring daily/monthly challenges.

usageGuide.title: Ranking
usageGuide.desc: See where you stand by character count, focus time, duel record, and typing speed.

usageGuide.title: Break
usageGuide.desc: Clear your head with a quick typing exercise, or browse the Free / Info / Recruiting boards.

faq.a: Yes, all core features are free. A paid tier (ad-free, etc.) is still in development.
There's no separate sign-up — just sign in with your Google account and you're in.

faq.q: Do I need to turn my camera on?
faq.a: No. The whole point of PoRoom is feeling like you're working together without a video call — no camera or microphone needed at all.

faq.q: Can other people see what I actually write?
faq.a: No. PoRoom only keeps records like character counts and focus time — the actual text of your manuscript is never entered or stored anywhere.

faq.q: Can I use a room by myself?
faq.a: Sure — you can sit in a room alone and just use the Pomodoro timer and character-count tracking. That said, PoRoom really shines once other people are there with you.
PomoWriter is a separate, free writing app, and PoRoom is an online study-room service. They're different products, but they pair well together, which is why we mention it.
Yes — no app to install, just open it in your mobile browser.

landing.footerCtaBody: All you need is a Google account — no credit card, no separate sign-up.
